record.narrative:
No claims are due for assessment. I registered a mix of follow-up refinements around the core accepted associations and a few targeted new biological probes, while avoiding another broad scan of already-null driver mutations. The accepted same-dataset associations are SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2, MSI-high with stronger WRN, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2, TP53 loss with weaker USP7, CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3. Several of these have QC-subset support, but the newly accepted PTEN-STAT3 association does not yet have QC/library-specificity checks. Therefore I registered PTEN-loss versus stronger dependency_STAT3 under high screen ROC, high Cas9 activity, non-Avana library, and higher aneuploidy. These are not new primary discoveries; they test whether the PTEN-STAT3 contrast is technically robust and not confined to a single assay-library context. I also registered PTEN loss versus stronger TMED10 as a specificity probe: if the accepted PTEN signal is genuinely associated with STAT3 and not broad PI3K-like dependency across secretory/growth pathways, TMED10 should not show a comparable strong effect. This is registered with uncertain expectation because TMED10 is only mechanistically adjacent, not strongly prior.

I prioritized locus/context refinements for the CDKN2A/MTAP-MDM2 axis. H140 already asks whether MTAP loss modifies the CDKN2A effect on MDM2; I added MTAP loss versus stronger MDM2 specifically among CDKN2A-intact lines. That helps distinguish whether the accepted MDM2 signal is CDKN2A/9p21-locus specific or whether MTAP co-deletion contributes independently when CDKN2A is intact. For the TP53-USP7 axis, I registered TP53 loss versus weaker USP7 among CDKN2A-loss lines because H121 showed the non-CDKN2A stratum is robust, but the complementary CDKN2A-loss stratum remains untested. This tests whether the TP53-USP7 contrast persists when the p53 pathway may be altered by CDKN2A/p14ARF loss. I also registered CDKN2A loss versus weaker USP7 as a new pathway-crosstalk hypothesis: CDKN2A loss can impair ARF-p53 signaling and may functionally mimic p53 loss for USP7 dependency. I used direction +1 because positive signed effect means weaker USP7 dependency in CDKN2A-loss lines; the USP7/NFE2L2 outcomes have near-zero means, so the approximate clinical-scale threshold is small, around 0.009, rather than around 0.025-0.030.

For WRN, I added MSI-high versus stronger dependency_WRN among non-MYC-amplified lines. MYC amplification can create replication and transcription stress and has already been involved in borderline WRN refinements; this tests whether the core MSI-WRN signal is not primarily carried by MYC-amplified lines. I also added STK11 loss versus stronger WRN as a broader stress-pathway probe, though I expect it may be null based on prior STK11 nulls. For KEAP1-NFE2L2, I registered the accepted contrast among higher-aneuploidy lines to test whether this very strong association remains contextually stable in genomically unstable cells. I activated previously registered QC refinements for TP53-USP7 and CDKN2A-MDM2 (H65, H66, H68, H69, H73) because confirming accepted core effects under screen-quality and library restrictions is more decision-relevant than further low-priority mutation scans. In the next appraise stage, I intend to reserve validation budget primarily for still-unvalidated core claims, starting with H8 MSI-high versus stronger WRN and then H6 SMARCA4 loss versus stronger SMARCA2, unless newly delivered scheduled validation or borderline QC results make another validation more informative. All proposed contrasts remain associations within the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),

their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

I registered a mix of follow-up refinements around the core accepted associations and a few targeted new biological probes, while avoiding another broad scan of already-null driver mutations. The accepted same-dataset associations are SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2, MSI-high with stronger WRN, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2, TP53 loss with weaker USP7, CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3. Several of these have QC-subset support, but the newly accepted PTEN-STAT3 association does not yet have QC/library-specificity checks. Therefore I registered PTEN-loss versus stronger dependency_STAT3 under high screen ROC, high Cas9 activity, non-Avana library, and higher aneuploidy. These are not new primary discoveries; they test whether the PTEN-STAT3 contrast is technically robust and not confined to a single assay-library context. I also registered PTEN loss versus stronger TMED10 as a specificity probe: if the accepted PTEN signal is genuinely associated with STAT3 and not broad PI3K-like dependency across secretory/growth pathways, TMED10 should not show a comparable strong effect. This is registered with uncertain expectation because TMED10 is only mechanistically adjacent, not strongly prior.\n\nI prioritized locus/context refinements for the CDKN2A/MTAP-MDM2 axis. H140 already asks whether MTAP loss modifies the CDKN2A effect on MDM2; I added MTAP loss versus stronger MDM2 specifically among CDKN2A-intact lines. That helps distinguish whether the accepted MDM2 signal is CDKN2A/9p21-locus specific or whether MTAP co-deletion contributes independently when CDKN2A is intact. For the TP53-USP7 axis, I registered TP53 loss versus weaker USP7 among CDKN2A-loss lines because H121 showed the non-CDKN2A stratum is robust, but the complementary CDKN2A-loss stratum remains untested. This tests whether the TP53-USP7 contrast persists when the p53 pathway may be altered by CDKN2A/p14ARF loss. I also registered CDKN2A loss versus weaker USP7 as a new pathway-crosstalk hypothesis: CDKN2A loss can impair ARF-p53 signaling and may functionally mimic p53 loss for USP7 dependency. I used direction +1 because positive signed effect means weaker USP7 dependency in CDKN2A-loss lines; the USP7/NFE2L2 outcomes have near-zero means, so the approximate clinical-scale threshold is small, around 0.009, rather than around 0.025-0.030.\n\nFor WRN, I added MSI-high versus stronger dependency_WRN among non-MYC-amplified lines. MYC amplification can create replication and transcription stress and has already been involved in borderline WRN refinements; this tests whether the core MSI-WRN signal is not primarily carried by MYC-amplified lines. I also added STK11 loss versus stronger WRN as a broader stress-pathway probe, though I expect it may be null based on prior STK11 nulls. For KEAP1-NFE2L2, I registered the accepted contrast among higher-aneuploidy lines to test whether this very strong association remains contextually stable in genomically unstable cells. I activated previously registered QC refinements for TP53-USP7 and CDKN2A-MDM2 (H65, H66, H68, H69, H73) because confirming accepted core effects under screen-quality and library restrictions is more decision-relevant than further low-priority mutation scans. In the next appraise stage, I intend to reserve validation budget primarily for still-unvalidated core claims, starting with H8 MSI-high versus stronger WRN and then H6 SMARCA4 loss versus stronger SMARCA2, unless newly delivered scheduled validation or borderline QC results make another validation more informative. Iteration 10/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
I assessed all 12 new discovery results using signed estimates, already oriented to the registered hypothesis direction. Approximate clinically meaningful scale was taken as about 10% of the relevant dependency-score magnitude: roughly 0.027 for MDM2, 0.025 for TMED10, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.030 for WRN, and very small thresholds for near-zero-centered USP7/NFE2L2 outcomes. These remain associations in the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not causal or external-generalization claims.

The TP53-loss association with weaker USP7 dependency is technically robust: high screen ROC (H65), high Cas9 activity (H66), and non-Avana library (H73) all give signed effects about 0.77-0.80 with lower bounds far above the USP7 clinical-scale threshold. Although non-Avana has small exposed n=43, the lower bound is still very large and the cell-count requirement is satisfied, so I accept and close these QC/context checks. The CDKN2A-loss association with stronger MDM2 dependency is similarly robust in high screen ROC and high Cas9 activity contexts (H68/H69), with signed effects around 0.14 and lower bounds well above the MDM2 threshold. The PTEN-loss association with stronger STAT3 dependency also remains large under high screen ROC and high Cas9 activity (H141/H142), with signed effects about 0.24-0.26 and lower bounds far above the STAT3 threshold.

Non-Avana PTEN-STAT3 (H143) is imprecise: point estimate 0.092, signed interval -0.062 to 0.246, exposed n=27. It neither confirms nor rules out a clinically meaningful effect, so I mark it unresolved and closed as a low-priority library-specificity check; it does not undermine the validated core PTEN-STAT3 result because QC and large-stratum evidence are much stronger.

Two specificity probes were negative in the registered direction. PTEN loss versus stronger TMED10 (H145) has signed interval upper bound 0.011, below the TMED10 threshold, so it does not support clinically meaningful stronger TMED10 dependency and supports locus/pathway specificity of the PTEN-STAT3 finding. The lower bound does allow a possible opposite TMED10 effect, but that was not the registered hypothesis and remains low priority. MTAP loss versus stronger MDM2 among CDKN2A-intact lines (H147) is near null (0.004; signed interval -0.018 to 0.026), just under the MDM2 threshold and not supporting a clinically meaningful independent MTAP effect when CDKN2A is intact. This is borderline in the upper tail, but the point estimate and interval width make any clinically meaningful stronger MDM2 effect unlikely, supporting CDKN2A/9p21 specificity rather than MTAP co-deletion contribution.

The MSI-high-WRN association is not confined to MYC-amplified lines: among MYC-negative lines, H148 has signed estimate 0.794 with lower bound 0.763, far above the WRN threshold. TP53 loss versus weaker USP7 also persists in the CDKN2A-loss stratum (H149), signed effect 0.808 with lower bound 0.767. These support the stability of core accepted associations in important co-genomic contexts.

I request independent validation for H8, MSI-high versus stronger dependency_WRN, because it is a core accepted association that remains unvalidated and is large enough to be scientifically decisive if it survives validation. Validation of H8 is more informative now than validating QC-subset refinements, especially given remaining budget and the need to shore up the few unvalidated core accepted claims.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
Synthesis assessment. The newly delivered validation materially supports two accepted findings and leaves one refinement unsupported. H74, testing CDKN2A loss versus stronger dependency_MDM2 in non-Avana library context, is now independently validated. The signed discovery estimate R56 was +0.126 [0.029, 0.222], and the independent validation R106 was +0.172 [0.037, 0.307]. Because H74 direction is -1, a positive signed value means CDKN2A-loss lines have more negative MDM2 dependency scores, i.e. stronger MDM2 dependency. The validation lower bound is above an approximate 10% clinical-scale threshold for MDM2 (~0.027), so I accept and close H74. H8, MSI-high versus stronger dependency_WRN, is also strongly validated: discovery R8 +0.790 [0.760, 0.819] and validation R131 +0.799 [0.754, 0.844], far above the WRN clinical-scale threshold (~0.030); I accept and close H8. H125, testing MYC amplification versus weaker dependency_WRN among MSI-negative, high-Cas9 lines, does not replicate clinically meaningfully. Discovery R102 was borderline +0.045 [0.010, 0.079], but independent validation R105 was +0.005 [-0.044, 0.054]. The validation interval includes both no effect and a moderate clinically meaningful weaker-WRN effect, and the point estimate is near null. Therefore I keep H125 unresolved and closed; it should not be treated as a supported association.

Current supported same-dataset associations. The robust evidence in this supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset supports six core predictor-dependency contrasts, all associations rather than causal claims. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger dependency_SMARCA2: large positive signed effects around 0.78-0.80 across the global claim and multiple quality-control/library/strain checks (H6/H18/H19/H30/H43/H118), with no compelling evidence of attenuation in these checks; global validation remains desirable. Second, MSI-high is associated with stronger dependency_WRN, now independently validated (H8 with R8 and R131), and robust across Avana, screen-quality, Cas9-quality, and MYC-negative strata. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker dependency_NFE2L2 (positive signed effects for direction +1 mean raw scores are less negative, i.e. weaker dependency), supported globally and in multiple quality-control/library/aneuploid/STK11-loss contexts, with screen-quality validation for H24. Fourth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency_USP7 (positive signed effects for direction +1 mean weaker USP7 dependency), independently validated for H49 and robust under high screen ROC, high Cas9 activity, non-Avana library, CDKN2A-intact, and CDKN2A-loss strata. Fifth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger dependency_MDM2 (negative raw MDM2 scores), accepted globally and in library/quality subcontexts, with independent validation for the overall claim H59 and the non-Avana refinement H74. Sixth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3, accepted globally and in PIK3CA-intact/PTEN-stratified main-effect checks, with independent validation for H103 and robust under high screen ROC and high Cas9 activity.

Negative, failed, or inconclusive evidence. Many nominal driver-gene hypotheses remain null or clinically uninformative: BRAF V600E versus dependency_BRAF, KRAS mutation versus dependency_KRAS, EGFR amplification versus dependency_EGFR, and ERBB2 amplification versus dependency_ERBB2 did not support clinically meaningful stronger dependency, and several cross-pathway probes were also near-null. MYC amplification effects on RPL11 and WRN were not robustly supported, including the MSI-negative/high-Cas9 WRN refinement H125 after validation. RB1 loss versus DHX9 showed an initial discovery signal but failed independent validation (H84/H90/R78). APC and SMAD4 probes for TMED10 and STAT3 did not support clinically meaningful stronger dependency. MTAP loss did not show a clinically meaningful independent effect on MDM2 among CDKN2A-intact lines, supporting CDKN2A/9p21 specificity rather than an independent MTAP effect. Most constructed research marker interactions were null or imprecise, and non-Avana PTEN-STAT3 was too imprecise to assess (H143) without undermining the validated core PTEN-STAT3 result.

Unresolved uncertainty. Remaining uncertainty is concentrated in co-genomic and context-dependent modification rather than the existence of the core main effects. Main effects can be very large while interaction strata remain imprecise: MTAP modification of CDKN2A-MDM2 (H140), PIK3CA or STK11 modification of PTEN-STAT3 (H119/H139), TP53 modification of KEAP1-NFE2L2 (H34/H72), and several MYC/MSI/Cas9 interaction refinements remain unresolved. The most informative next use of validation budget is to test the still-unvalidated core accepted associations, starting with H6 (SMARCA4 loss versus stronger dependency_SMARCA2) and then H17 or an equivalent KEAP1-NFE2L2 global claim if budget permits. If validation is not requested or unavailable, next discovery analyses should prioritize already active co-genomic refinements, especially H140 for MTAP-CDKN2A-MDM2 specificity and other active context checks for USP7/STAT3/WRN/NFE2L2, rather than additional broad driver-mutation scans. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations within the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR cohort, not causal inferences or externally generalizable claims.

prompt:
Iteration 11/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

I registered a mix of follow-up refinements around the core accepted associations and a few targeted new biological probes, while avoiding another broad scan of already-null driver mutations. The accepted same-dataset associations are SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2, MSI-high with stronger WRN, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2, TP53 loss with weaker USP7, CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3. Several of these have QC-subset support, but the newly accepted PTEN-STAT3 association does not yet have QC/library-specificity checks. Therefore I registered PTEN-loss versus stronger dependency_STAT3 under high screen ROC, high Cas9 activity, non-Avana library, and higher aneuploidy. These are not new primary discoveries; they test whether the PTEN-STAT3 contrast is technically robust and not confined to a single assay-library context. I also registered PTEN loss versus stronger TMED10 as a specificity probe: if the accepted PTEN signal is genuinely associated with STAT3 and not broad PI3K-like dependency across secretory/growth pathways, TMED10 should not show a comparable strong effect. This is registered with uncertain expectation because TMED10 is only mechanistically adjacent, not strongly prior.\n\nI prioritized locus/context refinements for the CDKN2A/MTAP-MDM2 axis. H140 already asks whether MTAP loss modifies the CDKN2A effect on MDM2; I added MTAP loss versus stronger MDM2 specifically among CDKN2A-intact lines. That helps distinguish whether the accepted MDM2 signal is CDKN2A/9p21-locus specific or whether MTAP co-deletion contributes independently when CDKN2A is intact. For the TP53-USP7 axis, I registered TP53 loss versus weaker USP7 among CDKN2A-loss lines because H121 showed the non-CDKN2A stratum is robust, but the complementary CDKN2A-loss stratum remains untested. This tests whether the TP53-USP7 contrast persists when the p53 pathway may be altered by CDKN2A/p14ARF loss. I also registered CDKN2A loss versus weaker USP7 as a new pathway-crosstalk hypothesis: CDKN2A loss can impair ARF-p53 signaling and may functionally mimic p53 loss for USP7 dependency. I used direction +1 because positive signed effect means weaker USP7 dependency in CDKN2A-loss lines; the USP7/NFE2L2 outcomes have near-zero means, so the approximate clinical-scale threshold is small, around 0.009, rather than around 0.025-0.030.\n\nFor WRN, I added MSI-high versus stronger dependency_WRN among non-MYC-amplified lines. MYC amplification can create replication and transcription stress and has already been involved in borderline WRN refinements; this tests whether the core MSI-WRN signal is not primarily carried by MYC-amplified lines. I also added STK11 loss versus stronger WRN as a broader stress-pathway probe, though I expect it may be null based on prior STK11 nulls. For KEAP1-NFE2L2, I registered the accepted contrast among higher-aneuploidy lines to test whether this very strong association remains contextually stable in genomically unstable cells. I activated previously registered QC refinements for TP53-USP7 and CDKN2A-MDM2 (H65, H66, H68, H69, H73) because confirming accepted core effects under screen-quality and library restrictions is more decision-relevant than further low-priority mutation scans. Approximate clinically meaningful scale was taken as about 10% of the relevant dependency-score magnitude: roughly 0.027 for MDM2, 0.025 for TMED10, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.030 for WRN, and very small thresholds for near-zero-centered USP7/NFE2L2 outcomes. These remain associations in the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not causal or external-generalization claims.\n\nThe TP53-loss association with weaker USP7 dependency is technically robust: high screen ROC (H65), high Cas9 activity (H66), and non-Avana library (H73) all give signed effects about 0.77-0.80 with lower bounds far above the USP7 clinical-scale threshold. Although non-Avana has small exposed n=43, the lower bound is still very large and the cell-count requirement is satisfied, so I accept and close these QC/context checks. The CDKN2A-loss association with stronger MDM2 dependency is similarly robust in high screen ROC and high Cas9 activity contexts (H68/H69), with signed effects around 0.14 and lower bounds well above the MDM2 threshold. The PTEN-loss association with stronger STAT3 dependency also remains large under high screen ROC and high Cas9 activity (H141/H142), with signed effects about 0.24-0.26 and lower bounds far above the STAT3 threshold.\n\nNon-Avana PTEN-STAT3 (H143) is imprecise: point estimate 0.092, signed interval -0.062 to 0.246, exposed n=27. It neither confirms nor rules out a clinically meaningful effect, so I mark it unresolved and closed as a low-priority library-specificity check; it does not undermine the validated core PTEN-STAT3 result because QC and large-stratum evidence are much stronger.\n\nTwo specificity probes were negative in the registered direction. PTEN loss versus stronger TMED10 (H145) has signed interval upper bound 0.011, below the TMED10 threshold, so it does not support clinically meaningful stronger TMED10 dependency and supports locus/pathway specificity of the PTEN-STAT3 finding. The lower bound does allow a possible opposite TMED10 effect, but that was not the registered hypothesis and remains low priority. MTAP loss versus stronger MDM2 among CDKN2A-intact lines (H147) is near null (0.004; signed interval -0.018 to 0.026), just under the MDM2 threshold and not supporting a clinically meaningful independent MTAP effect when CDKN2A is intact. This is borderline in the upper tail, but the point estimate and interval width make any clinically meaningful stronger MDM2 effect unlikely, supporting CDKN2A/9p21 specificity rather than MTAP co-deletion contribution.\n\nThe MSI-high-WRN association is not confined to MYC-amplified lines: among MYC-negative lines, H148 has signed estimate 0.794 with lower bound 0.763, far above the WRN threshold. TP53 loss versus weaker USP7 also persists in the CDKN2A-loss stratum (H149), signed effect 0.808 with lower bound 0.767. These support the stability of core accepted associations in important co-genomic contexts.\n\nI request independent validation for H8, MSI-high versus stronger dependency_WRN, because it is a core accepted association that remains unvalidated and is large enough to be scientifically decisive if it survives validation. Validation of H8 is more informative now than validating QC-subset refinements, especially given remaining budget and the need to shore up the few unvalidated core accepted claims.","synthesize":"Synthesis assessment. The newly delivered validation materially supports two accepted findings and leaves one refinement unsupported. H74, testing CDKN2A loss versus stronger dependency_MDM2 in non-Avana library context, is now independently validated. The signed discovery estimate R56 was +0.126 [0.029, 0.222], and the independent validation R106 was +0.172 [0.037, 0.307]. Because H74 direction is -1, a positive signed value means CDKN2A-loss lines have more negative MDM2 dependency scores, i.e. stronger MDM2 dependency. The validation lower bound is above an approximate 10% clinical-scale threshold for MDM2 (~0.027), so I accept and close H74. H8, MSI-high versus stronger dependency_WRN, is also strongly validated: discovery R8 +0.790 [0.760, 0.819] and validation R131 +0.799 [0.754, 0.844], far above the WRN clinical-scale threshold (~0.030); I accept and close H8. H125, testing MYC amplification versus weaker dependency_WRN among MSI-negative, high-Cas9 lines, does not replicate clinically meaningfully. Discovery R102 was borderline +0.045 [0.010, 0.079], but independent validation R105 was +0.005 [-0.044, 0.054]. The validation interval includes both no effect and a moderate clinically meaningful weaker-WRN effect, and the point estimate is near null. Therefore I keep H125 unresolved and closed; it should not be treated as a supported association.\n\nCurrent supported same-dataset associations. The robust evidence in this supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset supports six core predictor-dependency contrasts, all associations rather than causal claims. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger dependency_SMARCA2: large positive signed effects around 0.78-0.80 across the global claim and multiple quality-control/library/strain checks (H6/H18/H19/H30/H43/H118), with no compelling evidence of attenuation in these checks; global validation remains desirable. Second, MSI-high is associated with stronger dependency_WRN, now independently validated (H8 with R8 and R131), and robust across Avana, screen-quality, Cas9-quality, and MYC-negative strata. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker dependency_NFE2L2 (positive signed effects for direction +1 mean raw scores are less negative, i.e. weaker dependency), supported globally and in multiple quality-control/library/aneuploid/STK11-loss contexts, with screen-quality validation for H24. Fourth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency_USP7 (positive signed effects for direction +1 mean weaker USP7 dependency), independently validated for H49 and robust under high screen ROC, high Cas9 activity, non-Avana library, CDKN2A-intact, and CDKN2A-loss strata. Fifth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger dependency_MDM2 (negative raw MDM2 scores), accepted globally and in library/quality subcontexts, with independent validation for the overall claim H59 and the non-Avana refinement H74. Sixth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3, accepted globally and in PIK3CA-intact/PTEN-stratified main-effect checks, with independent validation for H103 and robust under high screen ROC and high Cas9 activity.\n\nNegative, failed, or inconclusive evidence. Many nominal driver-gene hypotheses remain null or clinically uninformative: BRAF V600E versus dependency_BRAF, KRAS mutation versus dependency_KRAS, EGFR amplification versus dependency_EGFR, and ERBB2 amplification versus dependency_ERBB2 did not support clinically meaningful stronger dependency, and several cross-pathway probes were also near-null. MYC amplification effects on RPL11 and WRN were not robustly supported, including the MSI-negative/high-Cas9 WRN refinement H125 after validation. RB1 loss versus DHX9 showed an initial discovery signal but failed independent validation (H84/H90/R78). APC and SMAD4 probes for TMED10 and STAT3 did not support clinically meaningful stronger dependency. I therefore registered follow-up comparisons that test whether the six core accepted same-dataset associations are stable in genomic instability, proliferation, inflammatory, and co-deletion contexts, and added two specificity probes. The high-aneuploidy refinements ask whether CDKN2A-loss versus stronger MDM2, TP53-loss versus weaker USP7, and SMARCA4-loss versus stronger SMARCA2 persist in genomically unstable lines. The KEAP1-NFE2L2 refinement fills the TP53-loss stratum, complementing the accepted TP53-intact analysis. The MSI-WRN refinement tests persistence among faster-growing lines. The PTEN-STAT3 interaction with high IFN-gamma signature tests whether the STAT3 association is amplified in an inflammatory/STAT3-relevant context. MTAP loss among CDKN2A-loss lines tests whether MTAP co-deletion changes MDM2 dependency beyond the accepted CDKN2A signal, and PTEN loss versus RPL11 tests whether PTEN association is STAT3-specific rather than a broad increase in essentiality. These are comparisons within the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset only, not causal or external-generalizability claims.

I therefore make no claim-status changes. I request 12 untested active discovery comparisons that focus on context dependence and specificity of the six accepted core associations rather than repeating the broad driver scans or previously tested QC refinements. The aneuploidy panel H144, H150, H152, H153, and H154 asks whether PTEN-loss versus stronger STAT3 dependency, KEAP1-loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency, CDKN2A-loss versus stronger MDM2 dependency, TP53-loss versus weaker USP7 dependency, and SMARCA4-loss versus stronger SMARCA2 dependency remain clinically large in genomically unstable lines. H155 and H157 test two important co-genomic or phenotypic strata for core accepted signals: KEAP1-NFE2L2 within TP53-loss lines, and MSI-high versus WRN dependency among faster-growing lines. H156 tests whether the PTEN-STAT3 association is modified by a high IFN-gamma signature, which is biologically relevant to STAT3 signaling. H158 and H140 follow up the CDKN2A/MTAP locus: H158 tests MTAP loss directly within CDKN2A-loss lines, and H140 tests MTAP modification of the CDKN2A-MDM2 effect in interaction form. This helps distinguish CDKN2A/9p21-specific MDM2 dependency from broader MTAP co-deletion effects. H146 tests CDKN2A loss against USP7 to assess whether the TP53-USP7 association is specific to TP53 loss or reflects a broader p53/9p21 pathway effect. H159 tests PTEN loss against RPL11 as a broad essentiality/specificity control. All requested comparisons are associations in the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset only; they are not causal claims or external-generalizability claims.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

record.narrative: The newly released independent validation for H6 is decisive. The validation estimate for SMARCA4 loss versus dependency_SMARCA2 is +0.790 with a signed lower bound +0.760 and upper bound +0.820 under the validation multiplicity threshold. Because H6 direction is -1, a positive signed value means SMARCA4-loss cells have more negative, i.e. stronger, SMARCA2 dependency scores than SMARCA4-intact cells. This agrees almost exactly with the discovery estimate from R6 and with the repeated library, screen-quality, Cas9-quality, and arid1a_loss/context refinements. I therefore accept H6 and close its investigation. With this validation, SMARCA4 loss versus stronger dependency_SMARCA2 is now one of the best-supported same-dataset associations, not merely a discovery-stage signal. The current scientific picture from this supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset is a set of large, reproducible predictor-dependent dependency-score contrasts. The strongest core associations are: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger dependency_SMARCA2; MSI-high is associated with much stronger dependency_WRN, independently validated; KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker dependency_NFE2L2; TP53 loss is associated with much weaker dependency_USP7, independently validated; CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger dependency_MDM2, independently validated; and PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3, independently validated. These conclusions are associations in the supplied dataset and should not be interpreted as causal or externally generalizable. The new validation also clarifies the boundary of supported specificity. PTEN loss versus dependency_RPL11 was rejected, supporting STAT3 specificity rather than a broad increase in essentiality. CDKN2A loss versus dependency_USP7 was near null and closed, supporting TP53 specificity of the USP7 result rather than a broad 9p21 or p53-pathway effect. MTAP-related probes remain unresolved: MTAP modification of the CDKN2A-MDM2 relationship and MTAP effect within CDKN2A-loss lines have suggestive positive signed point estimates but intervals that include no effect and clinically relevant opposite effects. Therefore MTAP co-deletion amplification is not supported as a dataset conclusion. The PTEN-STAT3 interaction with high IFN-gamma signature is accepted as a context modifier, but the main effects inside and outside the high-IFN subgroup still need decomposition. Negative driver-gene findings remain important: BRAF V600E did not support stronger dependency_BRAF, KRAS mutation did not support stronger dependency_KRAS, EGFR amplification did not support stronger dependency_EGFR, ERBB2 amplification did not support stronger dependency_ERBB2, and several cross-pathway or MYC-related probes were clinically uninformative. RB1 loss versus DHX9 had a discovery signal but failed independent validation, so it remains a negative or at least unreplicated result. The most informative next step is to preserve the validated core map while resolving two classes of uncertainty. First, if validation budget permits, independent validation of the global KEAP1 loss versus weaker dependency_NFE2L2 association would complete independent confirmation for all core associations, because that global KEAP1 claim remains the main unvalidated core result even though it has many accepted context refinements. Second, the newly registered analyses decompose the high-IFN PTEN-STAT3 interaction into main effects in high- and low-IFN strata, and they test whether MTAP loss adds to CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency in TP53 contexts and under high screen quality. These next analyses are more informative than additional broad driver scans because they target remaining modifiers and specificity rather than re-testing effects already accepted or rejected.

All requested comparisons are associations in the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset only; they are not causal claims or external-generalizability claims.","appraise":"I assessed the newly delivered discovery results using the already signed estimates and intervals. The signed scale is already oriented to each registered hypothesis, so positive values indicate support for the registered direction. For these dependency-score outcomes, approximate clinically meaningful scales are small for near-zero-centered outcomes and around 0.025 to 0.030 for outcomes with larger mean magnitudes such as MDM2, STAT3, WRN, SMARCA2, USP7, and NFE2L2 in the relevant strata. First, the high-aneuploidy context checks strongly support persistence of core accepted associations. H144, PTEN loss versus dependency_STAT3 among high-aneuploidy lines, has signed estimate +0.278 with signed lower bound +0.203, far above the STAT3 clinical scale, so it is accepted and closed. H150, KEAP1 loss versus weaker dependency_NFE2L2 among high-aneuploidy lines, has signed effect +0.794 with lower bound +0.766, far above the NFE2L2 clinical scale, so it is accepted. H152, CDKN2A loss versus stronger dependency_MDM2 among high-aneuploidy lines, has signed effect +0.102 with lower bound +0.051, above the MDM2 clinical scale, so it is accepted. H153, TP53 loss versus weaker dependency_USP7 among high-aneuploidy lines, has signed effect +0.800 with lower bound +0.774, so it is accepted. H154, SMARCA4 loss versus stronger dependency_SMARCA2 among high-aneuploidy lines, has signed effect +0.775 with lower bound +0.747, so it is accepted. These collectively show that genomic instability does not materially attenuate the main accepted associations in this dataset. Second, important co-genomic and phenotypic strata also support core effects. H155, KEAP1 loss versus weaker dependency_NFE2L2 within TP53-loss lines, has signed effect +0.810 with lower bound +0.763, supporting that the KEAP1-NFE2L2 association persists in a p53-altered stratum. H157, MSI-high versus stronger dependency_WRN among faster-growing lines, has signed effect +0.776 with lower bound +0.732, supporting persistence of the MSI-WRN association beyond screen quality and MYC contexts. Third, H156 is the most interesting new modifier result. PTEN loss versus dependency_STAT3 interacts with high IFN-gamma signature, with signed interaction estimate +0.212 and signed lower bound +0.094. Because direction is -1 and estimates are already signed, positive signed values indicate that the PTEN-loss contrast is more negative, i.e. stronger STAT3 dependency, in the high IFN-gamma subgroup relative to its complement. The lower bound is well above the STAT3 clinical scale, so this is accepted and closed as a dataset-specific context modification. However, it is an interaction refinement and does not replace the globally validated PTEN-STAT3 main effect. Fourth, the CDKN2A/MTAP specificity probes remain inconclusive. H140, MTAP modification of the CDKN2A-MDM2 interaction, has signed estimate +0.060 with interval -0.032 to +0.152. It is imprecise and includes zero and meaningful opposite directions. H158, MTAP loss versus stronger dependency_MDM2 within CDKN2A-loss lines, has signed estimate +0.064 with interval -0.025 to +0.153. The point estimate is above the MDM2 threshold but the lower bound does not exclude no effect or small opposite effects. These remain unresolved and active, but they should not be treated as supported co-deletion amplification without larger strata or validation. Fifth, two specificity probes were uninformative. H146, CDKN2A loss versus weaker dependency_USP7, is near null with signed interval -0.043 to +0.038; this neither supports nor rules out a small positive effect and is closed as unresolved because TP53-loss effects are far stronger and already validated. H159, PTEN loss versus stronger dependency_RPL11, is rejected: signed interval -0.037 to +0.011, with upper bound below the RPL11 clinical scale and point estimate actually favoring the opposite direction. This supports STAT3 specificity of PTEN loss rather than a broad essentiality effect. Overall, the new evidence strengthens six core same-dataset associations and adds a high-IFN modifier of PTEN-STAT3, while leaving MTAP co-deletion specificity unresolved. All conclusions are associations within the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not causal or external-generalizability claims. I request independent validation for H6, SMARCA4 loss versus stronger dependency_SMARCA2, because it is a core accepted association without independent validation and its magnitude is decisive if confirmed.","synthesize":"The newly released independent validation for H6 is decisive. The validation estimate for SMARCA4 loss versus dependency_SMARCA2 is +0.790 with a signed lower bound +0.760 and upper bound +0.820 under the validation multiplicity threshold. Because H6 direction is -1, a positive signed value means SMARCA4-loss cells have more negative, i.e. stronger, SMARCA2 dependency scores than SMARCA4-intact cells. This agrees almost exactly with the discovery estimate from R6 and with the repeated library, screen-quality, Cas9-quality, and arid1a_loss/context refinements. I therefore accept H6 and close its investigation. With this validation, SMARCA4 loss versus stronger dependency_SMARCA2 is now one of the best-supported same-dataset associations, not merely a discovery-stage signal. The current scientific picture from this supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset is a set of large, reproducible predictor-dependent dependency-score contrasts. The strongest core associations are: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger dependency_SMARCA2; MSI-high is associated with much stronger dependency_WRN, independently validated; KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker dependency_NFE2L2; TP53 loss is associated with much weaker dependency_USP7, independently validated; CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger dependency_MDM2, independently validated; and PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3, independently validated. These conclusions are associations in the supplied dataset and should not be interpreted as causal or externally generalizable. The new validation also clarifies the boundary of supported specificity. PTEN loss versus dependency_RPL11 was rejected, supporting STAT3 specificity rather than a broad increase in essentiality. CDKN2A loss versus dependency_USP7 was near null and closed, supporting TP53 specificity of the USP7 result rather than a broad 9p21 or p53-pathway effect. record.narrative: I assessed the newly delivered discovery evidence. All returned estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so a positive signed estimate supports the registered direction. For the dependency-score outcomes, the large accepted effects have signed lower bounds far above a 10% relative clinical threshold, so multiplicity and modest uncertainty do not materially threaten these conclusions. H160 and H161 are decisive decompositions of the PTEN-loss STAT3 association. In high IFN-gamma signature lines, the signed PTEN-loss contrast is +0.423 with signed lower bound +0.319; in the complementary low IFN-gamma stratum it is +0.211 with signed lower bound +0.152. Both are clinically large and statistically clear, but the high IFN-gamma stratum is about twice as large, explaining the accepted H156 interaction as a difference between two clinically meaningful stratum-specific main effects rather than absence of the main effect in one stratum. H165, H166, H167, H169, H170, H172, and H173 provide important context confirmations. MSI-high versus stronger WRN dependency remains very large in high-aneuploidy lines (+0.801 lower +0.761) and in slower-growing lines (+0.828 lower +0.782). KEAP1 loss versus weaker NFE2L2 dependency remains very large under high mutation burden (+0.798 lower +0.770). SMARCA4 loss versus stronger SMARCA2 dependency remains very large in low-aneuploidy lines (+0.791 lower +0.764) and high-stemness lines (+0.794 lower +0.754). PTEN loss versus stronger STAT3 dependency remains large in high-EMT lines (+0.378 lower +0.261) and high-stemness lines (+0.260 lower +0.155). These are accepted as dataset-context confirmations, not causal or generalizable claims. MTAP remains unresolved. H162 shows a positive signed point estimate of +0.065 for MTAP loss versus stronger MDM2 dependency within CDKN2A-loss/TP53-wild-type lines, above the approximate MDM2 clinical scale, but the interval includes no effect and clinically relevant opposite effects. H163 is uninformative because its TP53-loss/CDKN2A-loss MTAP cell sizes are below the analysis minimum. H175, PTEN loss versus WRN, is near null at +0.003, but its interval is wide enough to include small clinically relevant effects in either direction, so it is unresolved and deferred rather than conclusively rejected. I request independent validation for H162 because it is the last potentially clinically meaningful unresolved MTAP co-deletion signal and validation can either accept it or close the MTAP amplification hypothesis. All conclusions are associations in the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset only.

This validation interval does not show a multiplicity-corrected positive effect and is not near the MDM2 clinical significance scale. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
