record.narrative: No new independent validation was delivered and no response deadline is due, so no claim-status change is required in this synthesis. The voluntary validation budget is exhausted; the accepted evidence state therefore reflects the discovery results in the supplied dataset plus the independent validations already completed earlier in the ledger. Direction convention remains important: more negative dependency scores mean stronger dependency. For direction -1, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group or a stronger subgroup contrast; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. I interpret effects relative to the outcome scale and the supplied relative-significance criterion, while retaining the conservative practical view that very small absolute dependency-score differences are not scientifically decisive.   SUPPORTED DATASET-LEVEL ASSOCIATIONS: Six core associations are directionally coherent, scientifically meaningful in this lung-focused resource, and several have independent validation. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency: H6/R6 signed estimate +0.784, CI +0.765 to +0.803; independent validation R144 +0.790, CI +0.760 to +0.820. This effect is enormous relative to the dependency-score scale and persists across many quality-control, library, lineage, expression, and co-alteration strata. Negative specificity checks support pattern specificity: ARID1A main effects on SMARCA2 were rejected (H252/R231, H253/R232), and SMARCA4 loss was rejected for DHX9 (H278/R253). Second, MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency: H8/R8 +0.790, CI +0.760 to +0.819; validation R131 +0.799, CI +0.754 to +0.844. This is one of the largest and most robust effects in the dataset and survives multiple QC and context strata, including the high-mutation-burden check H285/R267 +0.780, CI +0.749 to +0.811. Low-mutation-burden restriction is structurally non-estimable rather than negative. Third, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: H49/R42 +0.802, CI +0.782 to +0.822; validation R52 +0.800, CI +0.769 to +0.831. The association is stable across Avana and non-Avana libraries, high Cas9 activity, adenocarcinoma, AXL-high, hypoxia-high, IFN-gamma-high, KEAP1-loss, and other strata. Interaction tests for lineage, MYC, STK11, KEAP1, IFN, and AXL did not support meaningful modification. Fourth, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency: H17/R7 +0.796, CI +0.776 to +0.816; high-quality-screen stratum H24/R19 +0.790 was independently validated by R39 +0.799, CI +0.759 to +0.839. The association persists across Avana, non-Avana, high Cas9, adenocarcinoma, STK11-intact, AXL-high, hypoxia-high, IFN-gamma-high, and PTEN-loss contexts. A meaningful KEAP1 by STK11 interaction was rejected (H271/R258). Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H103/R80 +0.267, CI +0.215 to +0.319; validation R92 +0.283, CI +0.208 to +0.358. This moderate effect is robust across serum, growth-rate, lineage, EMT, IFN, hypoxia, MYC-expression, and many co-alteration contexts. The accepted IFN-gamma-high interaction H156/R140 +0.212, CI +0.094 to +0.331, together with stratum contrasts H160/R145 +0.423 and H161/R146 +0.211, supports context enhancement in IFN-gamma-high lines, although the corresponding EMT interaction H179/R160 remains unresolved. Sixth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: H59/R48 +0.117, CI +0.082 to +0.152; validation R65 +0.116, CI +0.065 to +0.166. This is the smallest core effect but is directionally stable and replicated across library, lineage, MTAP contexts, and other strata. New context checks strengthen but do not fully resolve regional-copy-number specificity: H288/R266 among MTAP-loss TP53-intact lines is +0.162, CI +0.070 to +0.255, and H67/R274 among Avana lines is +0.116, CI +0.079 to +0.153; however, the lower bounds are near or below the conservative 0.10-unit benchmark, and H289 cannot distinguish CDKN2A-specific from broader 9p21 effects because the interaction is structurally non-estimable.   NEGATIVE FINDINGS: The tested driver-self dependency hypotheses are largely negative. BRAF V600E does not support stronger BRAF dependency (H1/R1), KRAS mutation does not support stronger KRAS dependency (H2/R2), EGFR amplification does not support stronger EGFR dependency with validation R13, and ERBB2 amplification does not support stronger ERBB2 dependency (H4/R4). Co-driver-restricted retests for BRAF, KRAS, EGFR, and ERBB2 remained null or near null. Cross-pathway tests are also mostly negative: ERBB2 amplification versus STAT3 dependency was rejected with validation R26; MYC amplification versus RPL11 dependency was rejected with validation R79; MYC amplification versus STAT3 dependency was near null; and MYC amplification versus WRN dependency in MSS or high-Cas9 contexts did not replicate. The initial RB1-loss versus DHX9 association did not survive independent validation, so H84 and H90 are rejected. MTAP-loss strict MDM2 associations were rejected or ambiguous, including H162/R147 plus validation R157 and H178/H251/R230. ARID1A loss did not independently support SMARCA2 dependency within SMARCA4-loss or SMARCA4-intact contexts. APC mutation in high-WNT lines did not support TMED10 dependency. Most effect-modification interaction tests for the core associations were rejected or near null, indicating that the core effects are broadly stable rather than highly context-dependent within the tested strata.   UNRESOLVED UNCERTAINTY: Several questions remain open but do not overturn the core findings. The PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency EMT interaction H179 is suggestive but imprecise and should not be upgraded to a supported context effect without larger external data. The IFN-gamma-high CDKN2A-MDM2 main effect H262/R241 +0.080, CI -0.004 to +0.164, and hypoxia-high CDKN2A-MDM2 effect H248/R229 +0.095, CI +0.020 to +0.171, are compatible with a real effect but remain below the practical benchmark. The 9p21-region question for CDKN2A-MDM2 cannot be answered cleanly in this dataset because CDKN2A loss is structurally entangled with low 9p21 copy number, as shown by non-estimable H289/R273. H143/R126 +0.092 and H203/R177 +0.098 are unresolved small context estimates. Constructed marker D/E/F main effects and several low-priority STK11 or marker-specific contrasts remain unresolved or unestimated; these are not evidence of absence. All results are dataset-level associations in a supplied lung-focused resource, many lines being adenocarcinoma, with constructed assays and many correlated genomic variables. They are not causal, therapeutic, or externally generalizable claims.   MOST INFORMATIVE NEXT ANALYSIS: The best in-dataset discovery follow-up has already been taken as far as high-value Welch comparisons allow. The single most informative next analysis would be external replication of the six core associations, especially CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency and PTEN-loss STAT3 IFN-gamma interaction, in independent cell-line or perturbation datasets. If region-level copy-number data are available, a joint model of CDKN2A, MTAP, and 9p21 copy number is needed to determine whether the CDKN2A-MDM2 association is CDKN2A-specific or reflects broader 9p21 co-deletion biology. Larger external samples would also be needed to resolve the PTEN-loss STAT3 EMT interaction and to test whether modest IFN or hypoxia context effects are genuine. Additional discovery testing inside this dataset would mostly increase multiplicity without solving the remaining precision or structural identifiability problems.

H288 is accepted: CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency among MTAP-loss and TP53-intact lines, signed estimate +0.162, 95% CI +0.070 to +0.255. The point estimate clearly exceeds the practical benchmark and excludes null, although the lower bound is below 0.10 absolute units and the cell size is modest. This supports the smallest core CDKN2A-MDM2 association beyond TP53-pathway context, but MTAP is genomically proximal to CDKN2A, so broad 9p21 co-deletion biology remains a plausible confounder. H289 was intended to test 9p21 context, but R273 is non-estimable because the interaction complement contains only one CDKN2A-loss observation; this is structural collinearity between CDKN2A loss and low 9p21 copy number, not evidence of absence, so it is closed unresolved. H67 is accepted: the CDKN2A-MDM2 association persists in Avana-library lines, signed estimate +0.116, 95% CI +0.079 to +0.153. The lower absolute bound is slightly below the 0.10-unit benchmark, but the estimate is directionally precise, exceeds benchmark in magnitude, and is consistent with the already accepted core and non-Avana library strata. H285 is accepted and resolves the high-mutation-burden check for MSI-high WRN dependency: signed estimate +0.780, 95% CI +0.749 to +0.811. This is a very large effect and excludes both null and benchmark. Low-mutation-burden tests remain non-estimable because MSI-high status is structurally tied to high mutation burden. H286-H292 accept PTEN-loss persistence for STAT3 dependency across serum and proliferation contexts. High serum: +0.286, CI +0.216 to +0.357. Low serum: +0.239, CI +0.163 to +0.316. Fast growth: +0.305, CI +0.196 to +0.414. Slow growth: +0.259, CI +0.176 to +0.342. Joint high-serum fast-growth: +0.327, CI +0.180 to +0.474. These are strong main-effect context checks; they do not prove synergistic modification because the corresponding serum and growth interactions H283/H284 remained imprecise and near null. H292 has smaller exposed n=41, so it is interpreted as robust consistency rather than a new interaction claim. H40, H41, and H55 are rejected. Direction convention remains important: more negative dependency scores mean stronger dependency. For direction -1, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group or a stronger subgroup contrast; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. I interpret effects relative to the outcome scale and the supplied relative-significance criterion, while retaining the conservative practical view that very small absolute dependency-score differences are not scientifically decisive.   SUPPORTED DATASET-LEVEL ASSOCIATIONS: Six core associations are directionally coherent, scientifically meaningful in this lung-focused resource, and several have independent validation. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency: H6/R6 signed estimate +0.784, CI +0.765 to +0.803; independent validation R144 +0.790, CI +0.760 to +0.820. This effect is enormous relative to the dependency-score scale and persists across many quality-control, library, lineage, expression, and co-alteration strata. Negative specificity checks support pattern specificity: ARID1A main effects on SMARCA2 were rejected (H252/R231, H253/R232), and SMARCA4 loss was rejected for DHX9 (H278/R253). Second, MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency: H8/R8 +0.790, CI +0.760 to +0.819; validation R131 +0.799, CI +0.754 to +0.844. This is one of the largest and most robust effects in the dataset and survives multiple QC and context strata, including the high-mutation-burden check H285/R267 +0.780, CI +0.749 to +0.811. Low-mutation-burden restriction is structurally non-estimable rather than negative. Third, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: H49/R42 +0.802, CI +0.782 to +0.822; validation R52 +0.800, CI +0.769 to +0.831. The association is stable across Avana and non-Avana libraries, high Cas9 activity, adenocarcinoma, AXL-high, hypoxia-high, IFN-gamma-high, KEAP1-loss, and other strata. Interaction tests for lineage, MYC, STK11, KEAP1, IFN, and AXL did not support meaningful modification. Fourth, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency: H17/R7 +0.796, CI +0.776 to +0.816; high-quality-screen stratum H24/R19 +0.790 was independently validated by R39 +0.799, CI +0.759 to +0.839. The association persists across Avana, non-Avana, high Cas9, adenocarcinoma, STK11-intact, AXL-high, hypoxia-high, IFN-gamma-high, and PTEN-loss contexts. A meaningful KEAP1 by STK11 interaction was rejected (H271/R258). Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H103/R80 +0.267, CI +0.215 to +0.319; validation R92 +0.283, CI +0.208 to +0.358. This moderate effect is robust across serum, growth-rate, lineage, EMT, IFN, hypoxia, MYC-expression, and many co-alteration contexts. The accepted IFN-gamma-high interaction H156/R140 +0.212, CI +0.094 to +0.331, together with stratum contrasts H160/R145 +0.423 and H161/R146 +0.211, supports context enhancement in IFN-gamma-high lines, although the corresponding EMT interaction H179/R160 remains unresolved. Sixth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: H59/R48 +0.117, CI +0.082 to +0.152; validation R65 +0.116, CI +0.065 to +0.166. This is the smallest core effect but is directionally stable and replicated across library, lineage, MTAP contexts, and other strata. New context checks strengthen but do not fully resolve regional-copy-number specificity: H288/R266 among MTAP-loss TP53-intact lines is +0.162, CI +0.070 to +0.255, and H67/R274 among Avana lines is +0.116, CI +0.079 to +0.153; however, the lower bounds are near or below the conservative 0.10-unit benchmark, and H289 cannot distinguish CDKN2A-specific from broader 9p21 effects because the interaction is structurally non-estimable.   NEGATIVE FINDINGS: The tested driver-self dependency hypotheses are largely negative. BRAF V600E does not support stronger BRAF dependency (H1/R1), KRAS mutation does not support stronger KRAS dependency (H2/R2), EGFR amplification does not support stronger EGFR dependency with validation R13, and ERBB2 amplification does not support stronger ERBB2 dependency (H4/R4). Co-driver-restricted retests for BRAF, KRAS, EGFR, and ERBB2 remained null or near null. Cross-pathway tests are also mostly negative: ERBB2 amplification versus STAT3 dependency was rejected with validation R26; MYC amplification versus RPL11 dependency was rejected with validation R79; MYC amplification versus STAT3 dependency was near null; and MYC amplification versus WRN dependency in MSS or high-Cas9 contexts did not replicate. The initial RB1-loss versus DHX9 association did not survive independent validation, so H84 and H90 are rejected. MTAP-loss strict MDM2 associations were rejected or ambiguous, including H162/R147 plus validation R157 and H178/H251/R230. ARID1A loss did not independently support SMARCA2 dependency within SMARCA4-loss or SMARCA4-intact contexts. APC mutation in high-WNT lines did not support TMED10 dependency. Most effect-modification interaction tests for the core associations were rejected or near null, indicating that the core effects are broadly stable rather than highly context-dependent within the tested strata.   UNRESOLVED UNCERTAINTY: Several questions remain open but do not overturn the core findings. The PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency EMT interaction H179 is suggestive but imprecise and should not be upgraded to a supported context effect without larger external data. The IFN-gamma-high CDKN2A-MDM2 main effect H262/R241 +0.080, CI -0.004 to +0.164, and hypoxia-high CDKN2A-MDM2 effect H248/R229 +0.095, CI +0.020 to +0.171, are compatible with a real effect but remain below the practical benchmark. The 9p21-region question for CDKN2A-MDM2 cannot be answered cleanly in this dataset because CDKN2A loss is structurally entangled with low 9p21 copy number, as shown by non-estimable H289/R273. H143/R126 +0.092 and H203/R177 +0.098 are unresolved small context estimates. Constructed marker D/E/F main effects and several low-priority STK11 or marker-specific contrasts remain unresolved or unestimated; these are not evidence of absence. All results are dataset-level associations in a supplied lung-focused resource, many lines being adenocarcinoma, with constructed assays and many correlated genomic variables. They are not causal, therapeutic, or externally generalizable claims.   MOST INFORMATIVE NEXT ANALYSIS: The best in-dataset discovery follow-up has already been taken as far as high-value Welch comparisons allow. The single most informative next analysis would be external replication of the six core associations, especially CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency and PTEN-loss STAT3 IFN-gamma interaction, in independent cell-line or perturbation datasets. If region-level copy-number data are available, a joint model of CDKN2A, MTAP, and 9p21 copy number is needed to determine whether the CDKN2A-MDM2 association is CDKN2A-specific or reflects broader 9p21 co-deletion biology. Larger external samples would also be needed to resolve the PTEN-loss STAT3 EMT interaction and to test whether modest IFN or hypoxia context effects are genuine. Additional discovery testing inside this dataset would mostly increase multiplicity without solving the remaining precision or structural identifiability problems."}}

record.narrative: No validations remain, so this explore stage is used for targeted discovery refinements rather than replication. I first reassessed H179 and accept it now: the PTEN-loss STAT3-dependency interaction with high EMT has signed estimate +0.141 with 95% CI +0.011 to +0.271. The interval excludes null and the point estimate exceeds the conservative 0.10 absolute dependency-unit benchmark used for these outcomes. I nevertheless interpret this as a dataset-level context-enhancement signal, not as proof of a general biological interaction, because the lower bound is close to null and many related EMT interaction estimates have been imprecise. The new proposals are designed to test robustness and specificity of the core accepted associations across chromosomal-instability contexts and to complete several unresolved biological panels. Ploidy is a genome-wide instability measure that is correlated with, but not identical to, aneuploidy score and mutation burden. I therefore register SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2, MSI-high WRN, TP53-loss USP7, KEAP1-loss NFE2L2, PTEN-loss STAT3, and CDKN2A-loss MDM2 main effects in high-ploidy lines, plus CDKN2A-loss MDM2 in low-ploidy lines. If these effects persist, the core associations are less likely to be artifacts of chromosomal instability; if the smallest CDKN2A-MDM2 effect disappears in low-ploidy or appears only in high-ploidy, that would indicate that regional/genomic context is important. For PTEN-loss STAT3, I add an interaction with MYC-high expression, because PTEN/PI3K and MYC pathways can cooperate with STAT3; a positive signed interaction under direction -1 would indicate a stronger PTEN-loss association in MYC-high lines, while a near-null result would keep the accepted IFN-gamma interaction as the main context signal. For KEAP1-loss NFE2L2, I test the accepted weaker-dependency direction in EMT-high lines as a state-specific stress-context robustness check. For KIF18A, I test whether RB1 loss has stronger association with KIF18A dependency in high-ploidy lines, reflecting a possible mitotic/aneuploidy-stress context. For TMED10, I test MYC amplification to complete the MYC transcription/translation/secretion panel; a near-null result would support pathway specificity, while a large positive signed effect would suggest a secretory-pathway vulnerability in MYC-amplified lines. Direction convention: more negative dependency scores are stronger dependency. For direction -1, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group or a stronger exposed-minus-comparator contrast in the target subgroup. For direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group or a stronger subgroup contrast in the weaker-dependency direction. All new claims remain dataset-level associations in the supplied lung-focused resource and are not causal, therapeutic, or externally generalizable claims.

H288 is accepted: CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency among MTAP-loss and TP53-intact lines, signed estimate +0.162, 95% CI +0.070 to +0.255. The point estimate clearly exceeds the practical benchmark and excludes null, although the lower bound is below 0.10 absolute units and the cell size is modest. This supports the smallest core CDKN2A-MDM2 association beyond TP53-pathway context, but MTAP is genomically proximal to CDKN2A, so broad 9p21 co-deletion biology remains a plausible confounder. H289 was intended to test 9p21 context, but R273 is non-estimable because the interaction complement contains only one CDKN2A-loss observation; this is structural collinearity between CDKN2A loss and low 9p21 copy number, not evidence of absence, so it is closed unresolved. H67 is accepted: the CDKN2A-MDM2 association persists in Avana-library lines, signed estimate +0.116, 95% CI +0.079 to +0.153. The lower absolute bound is slightly below the 0.10-unit benchmark, but the estimate is directionally precise, exceeds benchmark in magnitude, and is consistent with the already accepted core and non-Avana library strata. H285 is accepted and resolves the high-mutation-burden check for MSI-high WRN dependency: signed estimate +0.780, 95% CI +0.749 to +0.811. This is a very large effect and excludes both null and benchmark. Low-mutation-burden tests remain non-estimable because MSI-high status is structurally tied to high mutation burden. H286-H292 accept PTEN-loss persistence for STAT3 dependency across serum and proliferation contexts. High serum: +0.286, CI +0.216 to +0.357. Low serum: +0.239, CI +0.163 to +0.316. Fast growth: +0.305, CI +0.196 to +0.414. Slow growth: +0.259, CI +0.176 to +0.342. Joint high-serum fast-growth: +0.327, CI +0.180 to +0.474. These are strong main-effect context checks; they do not prove synergistic modification because the corresponding serum and growth interactions H283/H284 remained imprecise and near null. H292 has smaller exposed n=41, so it is interpreted as robust consistency rather than a new interaction claim. H40, H41, and H55 are rejected. KRAS-adenocarcinoma KRAS dependency is +0.012, CI -0.009 to +0.032; ERBB2-amplified adenocarcinoma ERBB2 dependency is -0.012, CI -0.045 to +0.020; MYC amplification versus STAT3 dependency is -0.004, CI -0.034 to +0.026. All are near null, interval endpoints exclude meaningful dependency differences, and these are consistent with the prior negative driver-self and cross-pathway tests. Direction convention remains important: more negative dependency scores mean stronger dependency. For direction -1, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group or a stronger subgroup contrast; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed group. I interpret effects relative to the outcome scale and the supplied relative-significance criterion, while retaining the conservative practical view that very small absolute dependency-score differences are not scientifically decisive.   SUPPORTED DATASET-LEVEL ASSOCIATIONS: Six core associations are directionally coherent, scientifically meaningful in this lung-focused resource, and several have independent validation. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency: H6/R6 signed estimate +0.784, CI +0.765 to +0.803; independent validation R144 +0.790, CI +0.760 to +0.820. This effect is enormous relative to the dependency-score scale and persists across many quality-control, library, lineage, expression, and co-alteration strata. Negative specificity checks support pattern specificity: ARID1A main effects on SMARCA2 were rejected (H252/R231, H253/R232), and SMARCA4 loss was rejected for DHX9 (H278/R253). Second, MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency: H8/R8 +0.790, CI +0.760 to +0.819; validation R131 +0.799, CI +0.754 to +0.844. This is one of the largest and most robust effects in the dataset and survives multiple QC and context strata, including the high-mutation-burden check H285/R267 +0.780, CI +0.749 to +0.811. Low-mutation-burden restriction is structurally non-estimable rather than negative. Third, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: H49/R42 +0.802, CI +0.782 to +0.822; validation R52 +0.800, CI +0.769 to +0.831. The association is stable across Avana and non-Avana libraries, high Cas9 activity, adenocarcinoma, AXL-high, hypoxia-high, IFN-gamma-high, KEAP1-loss, and other strata. Interaction tests for lineage, MYC, STK11, KEAP1, IFN, and AXL did not support meaningful modification. Fourth, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency: H17/R7 +0.796, CI +0.776 to +0.816; high-quality-screen stratum H24/R19 +0.790 was independently validated by R39 +0.799, CI +0.759 to +0.839. The association persists across Avana, non-Avana, high Cas9, adenocarcinoma, STK11-intact, AXL-high, hypoxia-high, IFN-gamma-high, and PTEN-loss contexts. A meaningful KEAP1 by STK11 interaction was rejected (H271/R258). Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H103/R80 +0.267, CI +0.215 to +0.319; validation R92 +0.283, CI +0.208 to +0.358. This moderate effect is robust across serum, growth-rate, lineage, EMT, IFN, hypoxia, MYC-expression, and many co-alteration contexts. The accepted IFN-gamma-high interaction H156/R140 +0.212, CI +0.094 to +0.331, together with stratum contrasts H160/R145 +0.423 and H161/R146 +0.211, supports context enhancement in IFN-gamma-high lines, although the corresponding EMT interaction H179/R160 remains unresolved. Sixth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: H59/R48 +0.117, CI +0.082 to +0.152; validation R65 +0.116, CI +0.065 to +0.166. This is the smallest core effect but is directionally stable and replicated across library, lineage, MTAP contexts, and other strata. New context checks strengthen but do not fully resolve regional-copy-number specificity: H288/R266 among MTAP-loss TP53-intact lines is +0.162, CI +0.070 to +0.255, and H67/R274 among Avana lines is +0.116, CI +0.079 to +0.153; however, the lower bounds are near or below the conservative 0.10-unit benchmark, and H289 cannot distinguish CDKN2A-specific from broader 9p21 effects because the interaction is structurally non-estimable.   NEGATIVE FINDINGS: The tested driver-self dependency hypotheses are largely negative. Negative specificity checks support pattern specificity: ARID1A main effects on SMARCA2 were rejected (H252/R231, H253/R232), and SMARCA4 loss was rejected for DHX9 (H278/R253). Second, MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency: H8/R8 +0.790, CI +0.760 to +0.819; validation R131 +0.799, CI +0.754 to +0.844. This is one of the largest and most robust effects in the dataset and survives multiple QC and context strata, including the high-mutation-burden check H285/R267 +0.780, CI +0.749 to +0.811. Low-mutation-burden restriction is structurally non-estimable rather than negative. Third, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: H49/R42 +0.802, CI +0.782 to +0.822; validation R52 +0.800, CI +0.769 to +0.831. The association is stable across Avana and non-Avana libraries, high Cas9 activity, adenocarcinoma, AXL-high, hypoxia-high, IFN-gamma-high, KEAP1-loss, and other strata. Interaction tests for lineage, MYC, STK11, KEAP1, IFN, and AXL did not support meaningful modification. Fourth, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency: H17/R7 +0.796, CI +0.776 to +0.816; high-quality-screen stratum H24/R19 +0.790 was independently validated by R39 +0.799, CI +0.759 to +0.839. The association persists across Avana, non-Avana, high Cas9, adenocarcinoma, STK11-intact, AXL-high, hypoxia-high, IFN-gamma-high, and PTEN-loss contexts. A meaningful KEAP1 by STK11 interaction was rejected (H271/R258). Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H103/R80 +0.267, CI +0.215 to +0.319; validation R92 +0.283, CI +0.208 to +0.358. This moderate effect is robust across serum, growth-rate, lineage, EMT, IFN, hypoxia, MYC-expression, and many co-alteration contexts. The accepted IFN-gamma-high interaction H156/R140 +0.212, CI +0.094 to +0.331, together with stratum contrasts H160/R145 +0.423 and H161/R146 +0.211, supports context enhancement in IFN-gamma-high lines, although the corresponding EMT interaction H179/R160 remains unresolved. Sixth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: H59/R48 +0.117, CI +0.082 to +0.152; validation R65 +0.116, CI +0.065 to +0.166. This is the smallest core effect but is directionally stable and replicated across library, lineage, MTAP contexts, and other strata. New context checks strengthen but do not fully resolve regional-copy-number specificity: H288/R266 among MTAP-loss TP53-intact lines is +0.162, CI +0.070 to +0.255, and H67/R274 among Avana lines is +0.116, CI +0.079 to +0.153; however, the lower bounds are near or below the conservative 0.10-unit benchmark, and H289 cannot distinguish CDKN2A-specific from broader 9p21 effects because the interaction is structurally non-estimable.   NEGATIVE FINDINGS: The tested driver-self dependency hypotheses are largely negative. BRAF V600E does not support stronger BRAF dependency (H1/R1), KRAS mutation does not support stronger KRAS dependency (H2/R2), EGFR amplification does not support stronger EGFR dependency with validation R13, and ERBB2 amplification does not support stronger ERBB2 dependency (H4/R4). Co-driver-restricted retests for BRAF, KRAS, EGFR, and ERBB2 remained null or near null. Cross-pathway tests are also mostly negative: ERBB2 amplification versus STAT3 dependency was rejected with validation R26; MYC amplification versus RPL11 dependency was rejected with validation R79; MYC amplification versus STAT3 dependency was near null; and MYC amplification versus WRN dependency in MSS or high-Cas9 contexts did not replicate. The initial RB1-loss versus DHX9 association did not survive independent validation, so H84 and H90 are rejected. MTAP-loss strict MDM2 associations were rejected or ambiguous, including H162/R147 plus validation R157 and H178/H251/R230. ARID1A loss did not independently support SMARCA2 dependency within SMARCA4-loss or SMARCA4-intact contexts. APC mutation in high-WNT lines did not support TMED10 dependency. Most effect-modification interaction tests for the core associations were rejected or near null, indicating that the core effects are broadly stable rather than highly context-dependent within the tested strata.   UNRESOLVED UNCERTAINTY: Several questions remain open but do not overturn the core findings. The PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency EMT interaction H179 is suggestive but imprecise and should not be upgraded to a supported context effect without larger external data. The IFN-gamma-high CDKN2A-MDM2 main effect H262/R241 +0.080, CI -0.004 to +0.164, and hypoxia-high CDKN2A-MDM2 effect H248/R229 +0.095, CI +0.020 to +0.171, are compatible with a real effect but remain below the practical benchmark. The 9p21-region question for CDKN2A-MDM2 cannot be answered cleanly in this dataset because CDKN2A loss is structurally entangled with low 9p21 copy number, as shown by non-estimable H289/R273. H143/R126 +0.092 and H203/R177 +0.098 are unresolved small context estimates. Constructed marker D/E/F main effects and several low-priority STK11 or marker-specific contrasts remain unresolved or unestimated; these are not evidence of absence. All results are dataset-level associations in a supplied lung-focused resource, many lines being adenocarcinoma, with constructed assays and many correlated genomic variables. They are not causal, therapeutic, or externally generalizable claims.   MOST INFORMATIVE NEXT ANALYSIS: The best in-dataset discovery follow-up has already been taken as far as high-value Welch comparisons allow. The single most informative next analysis would be external replication of the six core associations, especially CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency and PTEN-loss STAT3 IFN-gamma interaction, in independent cell-line or perturbation datasets. If region-level copy-number data are available, a joint model of CDKN2A, MTAP, and 9p21 copy number is needed to determine whether the CDKN2A-MDM2 association is CDKN2A-specific or reflects broader 9p21 co-deletion biology. Larger external samples would also be needed to resolve the PTEN-loss STAT3 EMT interaction and to test whether modest IFN or hypoxia context effects are genuine. Additional discovery testing inside this dataset would mostly increase multiplicity without solving the remaining precision or structural identifiability problems."}}

record.narrative: Validation capacity is exhausted, so this appraisal treats all newly delivered results as discovery-level context and specificity analyses in the supplied dataset, not external replication. Estimates are already signed to the claim direction. For direction -1, a positive estimate indicates stronger dependency in the exposed group or a stronger subgroup contrast; for direction +1, a positive estimate indicates weaker dependency in the exposed group. I continue to use an absolute dependency-score difference near 0.10 as a conservative practical benchmark, but also weigh interval precision, prior replication, and the very large scales of several core effects. H89 is rejected: ERBB2 amplification is essentially null for EGFR dependency, signed estimate -0.003, 95% CI -0.030 to +0.023; this is far below the practical benchmark and inconsistent with a meaningful cross-receptor tyrosine kinase association. H293-H297 and H301 strongly support persistence of the core accepted associations in stress/genome-instability contexts: SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 in high ploidy +0.772, CI +0.745 to +0.799; MSI-high WRN in high ploidy +0.771, CI +0.728 to +0.814; TP53-loss USP7 in high ploidy +0.793, CI +0.765 to +0.822; KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 in high ploidy +0.808, CI +0.779 to +0.838; PTEN-loss STAT3 in high ploidy +0.294, CI +0.218 to +0.370; and KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 in EMT-high lines +0.803, CI +0.763 to +0.843. These are large or moderate effects whose intervals exclude both null and the practical benchmark. H298 and H299 accept CDKN2A-loss MDM2 associations in high ploidy +0.107, CI +0.060 to +0.154, and low ploidy +0.128, CI +0.076 to +0.179. The point estimates exceed the practical benchmark and intervals exclude zero; their lower bounds are below 0.10, so they are interpreted as consistent, replicated context checks rather than newly decisive interactions. H300, H302, and H303 are rejected: PTEN-loss STAT3 interaction with MYC-high expression +0.031, CI -0.074 to +0.135; RB1-loss KIF18A interaction with high ploidy +0.009, CI -0.046 to +0.065; and MYC amplification versus TMED10 dependency +0.009, CI -0.014 to +0.031. These are near-null, imprecise, and do not support additional biological modification beyond the already tested contexts. Overall, these results strengthen dataset-level robustness of the six core associations across ploidy and selected stress-state contexts, while further narrowing the set of supported additional pathway interactions. No causal, therapeutic, or externally generalizable conclusions are supported.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and independent-validation capacity is exhausted. This analyze stage requests the 12 registered active discovery analyses that currently have no evidence: H304-H315. They test robustness and context specificity of the six core dataset-level associations: SMARCA4-loss stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high stronger WRN dependency, TP53-loss weaker USP7 dependency, KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 dependency, and CDKN2A-loss stronger MDM2 dependency. H304-H306 probe SMARCA2 dependency under MYC-high expression, an interaction between SMARCA4 loss and MTAP loss, and an MTAP main effect among SMARCA4-intact lines as a specificity check. H307-H308 probe WRN dependency in MSI-high lines by SLFN11-high expression and high serum culture context. H309-H310 probe context interactions for the accepted weaker-dependency effects for USP7 and NFE2L2 under hypoxia and stemness. H311-H312 probe PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency under high ploidy and SLFN11-high expression. H313-H314 probe CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency under high MYC expression and faster growth. H315 probes SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency under high serum culture context. These are Welch discovery tests in the supplied dataset, not independent validation. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger exposed-group dependency or a stronger subgroup contrast; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the accepted weaker-dependency pattern is stronger in the target context. Near-null estimates support robustness without context specificity, clear positive estimates above the practical benchmark support context amplification, and negative estimates would indicate attenuation or reversed interaction. All conclusions remain dataset-level associations in this lung-focused resource and do not establish causality, therapeutic relevance, or external generalizability.

record.narrative: All twelve newly delivered comparisons are discovery analyses in the supplied dataset; independent validation capacity is exhausted, so none can be treated as external replication. Estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. I evaluate them as pre-registered context/specificity or interaction probes, not causal tests. Given the large number of exploratory comparisons and the arbitrary dependency-score scale, I continue to use an approximately 0.10 absolute dependency-unit practical benchmark as a conservative guide, while considering interval precision and consistency with the established core effects. H304 rejects meaningful enhancement of SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency in MYC-high lines: the signed interaction is only +0.023, with a 95% interval from -0.016 to +0.062, entirely too small to support robust context amplification. H305 and H306 also reject independent context or specificity threats to the SMARCA2 result: the SMARCA4-loss by MTAP-loss interaction is near null (-0.006, interval -0.056 to +0.045), and MTAP loss among SMARCA4-intact lines has essentially no main effect on SMARCA2 dependency (+0.006, interval -0.017 to +0.029). These null results support, rather than undermine, the interpretation that the large SMARCA2 association is more specific to SMARCA4 loss than to generic 9p21-region MTAP loss. H307 is the strongest new signal: MSI-high WRN dependency appears somewhat stronger in SLFN11-high lines, signed interaction +0.061 with interval +0.002 to +0.119. It excludes the null and is biologically suggestive, but the point estimate is below the practical benchmark, the interval is wide, and the claim is one of many exploratory interaction tests; I therefore leave it unresolved and close it. H308 rejects high-serum modification of the WRN MSI-high effect (-0.012, interval -0.072 to +0.048). H309 and H310 reject meaningful hypoxia and stemness modification of the established weaker-dependency associations for USP7/TP53 and NFE2L2/KEAP1: signed interactions are +0.009 (-0.036 to +0.055) and -0.002 (-0.049 to +0.046). These support robustness of the core effects but not context amplification. H311 remains unresolved: PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency may be modestly stronger in high-ploidy lines (signed interaction +0.058, interval -0.046 to +0.161), but the estimate is imprecise and compatible with null. H312 rejects meaningful SLFN11 modification of PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency (+0.010, interval -0.095 to +0.114): despite the wide interval, the point estimate is essentially null. H313 and H314 reject MYC-high and faster-growth modification of the CDKN2A-loss MDM2 association: signed interactions are near null and compatible with no context-specific change. H315 rejects high-serum modification of SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency (+0.039, interval -0.001 to +0.078); although statistically borderline, the effect is too small and imprecise to call scientifically meaningful. Overall, these new results largely reinforce the six core dataset-level associations as robust to several expression, co-alteration, ploidy, growth, and culture contexts, while identifying no reliable additional context-specific enhancement beyond the already established IFN-gamma and EMT hints for PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency. The remaining uncertainty is concentrated in modest, imprecise interactions, especially H307 and H311, which should not be converted into accepted biological mechanisms without external replication.

H179 is accepted as a suggestive EMT context enhancement for PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency, but its interval is imprecise. SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H6/R6 +0.784 CI 0.765 to 0.803; R144 validation +0.790 CI 0.760 to 0.820), stable across QC, library, lineage, expression, co-alteration and context strata. Specificity is supported by near-null ARID1A effects on SMARCA2 (H252/R231; H253/R232), near-null SMARCA4 effect on DHX9 (H278/R253), and near-null SMARCA4-loss by MTAP interaction and MTAP main effect among SMARCA4-intact lines (H305/R291; H306/R292). MSI-high is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency (H8/R8 +0.790 CI 0.760 to 0.819; R131 +0.799 CI 0.754 to 0.844), including high mutation burden (H285/R267 +0.780 CI 0.749 to 0.811). TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency (H49/R42 +0.802 CI 0.782 to 0.822; R52 +0.800 CI 0.769 to 0.831), robust across library, QC, lineage, ploidy, and expression contexts. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H17/R7 +0.796 CI 0.776 to 0.816; high-quality subset H24/R19 +0.790 and R39 validation +0.799 CI 0.759 to 0.839), stable across strata. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency (H103/R80 +0.267 CI 0.215 to 0.319; R92 +0.283 CI 0.208 to 0.358). Dataset-level context enhancement is strongest in IFN-gamma-high lines (H156/R140 +0.212 CI 0.094 to 0.331) and EMT-high lines (H179/R160 +0.141 CI 0.011 to 0.271), although the EMT estimate is imprecise and should remain a dataset-level signal. CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency (H59/R48 +0.117 CI 0.082 to 0.152; R65 +0.116 CI 0.065 to 0.166; non-Avana H74/R56 plus R106 +0.172 CI 0.037 to 0.307). This is the smallest core effect but reproducible across strata, including the MTAP-loss TP53-intact subset (H288/R266 +0.162 CI 0.070 to 0.255).

Negative findings. The intuitive self-driver dependency hypotheses are unsupported: BRAF V600E does not strengthen BRAF dependency (H1/R1; H273/R248); KRAS mutation does not strengthen KRAS dependency (H2/R2; H274/R249); EGFR amplification does not strengthen EGFR dependency and did not validate (H3/R3; R13); ERBB2 amplification does not strengthen ERBB2 dependency (H4/R4; H41/R276). Cross-receptor and driver co-alteration analyses are mostly null: ERBB2 amplification with STAT3 dependency (H15/R21; validation R26), ERBB2 amplification with EGFR dependency (H89/R278), EGFR amplification with ERBB2 dependency (H57/R46), MYC amplification with TMED10 dependency (H303/R289), RB1 ploidy context for KIF18A (H302/R288), and MYC interaction for PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency (H300/R286). The initial RB1-loss DHX9 signal did not independently replicate (H84/R61+R78; H90/R61+R78). MTAP loss generally does not provide an independent MDM2 effect after conditioning on CDKN2A, and several MTAP conditional estimates are null or imprecise (H162/R147 plus R157; H178/H251/R230). Constructed D/E/F markers do not show consistent core associations. Recent robustness checks H304-H315 mostly reject context modification for the core associations, including SMARCA2 under high serum or MYC-high, WRN under high serum, USP7/NFE2L2 under hypoxia or stemness, STAT3 under SLFN11-high or ploidy, and MDM2 under MYC-high or faster growth, except for two unresolved probes below.

Unresolved uncertainty. H307 is a suggestive MSI-high WRN by SLFN11-high interaction (signed +0.061 CI 0.002 to 0.119) but is below the practical benchmark, imprecise, and exploratory; I leave it unresolved and closed. H311 is a suggestive high-ploidy interaction for PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency (signed +0.058 CI -0.046 to 0.161) but compatible with null; I leave it unresolved and closed. Several accepted PTEN-STAT3 context effects remain imprecise, especially EMT H179, and AXL, stemness, TP53, and KEAP1 contexts remain unresolved or near-null. CDKN2A-MDM2 cannot be cleanly separated from 9p21 copy-number biology because H289/R273 is non-estimable due sparse cells. WRN in low mutation burden is non-estimable rather than negative (H281/R262). All conclusions are dataset-level associations in this supplied lung-focused resource with constructed assays and correlated genomic features; they do not establish causality, therapeutic relevance, or external generalizability.

Most informative next analysis. With internal validation capacity exhausted, the highest-value next work is external replication of the six core associations, especially CDKN2A-loss MDM2 dependency and PTEN-loss STAT3 context modulation. External data should jointly model CDKN2A, MTAP, and 9p21 copy-number/loss states to distinguish locus tagging from CDKN2A-specific biology. Larger replication samples are also needed to resolve the WRN SLFN11 interaction and STAT3 ploidy, EMT, and IFN-gamma context effects using joint interaction or subgroup-model analyses.

record.narrative: With independent validation capacity exhausted and no assessments due, this final explore stage registers discovery-level follow-up tests that target the most scientifically valuable remaining uncertainties: whether the accepted core associations are robust in the dominant adherent culture context under high-quality screen criteria, whether imprecise context interactions become interpretable after restricting to high-quality screens, and whether the CDKN2A-loss MDM2 association persists outside low 9p21 copy-number contexts. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger exposed-group dependency or a stronger subgroup contrast; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the accepted weaker-dependency pattern is stronger. Estimates are already signed to the registered direction. I treat approximate absolute dependency differences above about 0.10 dependency units, together with interval precision and consistency with the established core effects, as practically meaningful; core associations are much larger. The SLFN11 refinements of H307 ask whether MSI-high WRN dependency remains strong and perhaps enhanced in SLFN11-high, high-quality screens; a positive interaction above the practical benchmark would support a dataset-level context signal, while a near-null result would favor treating H307 as exploratory noise or a small imprecise effect. The ploidy refinement of H311 is deliberately more conservative because the original signal was positive but compatible with null. The IFN-gamma and EMT refinements of accepted PTEN-loss STAT3 context effects test whether the accepted enhancement persists when technical screen noise is reduced. The CDKN2A-loss MDM2 analysis restricted to copy_number_9p21 not below the median tests whether the MDM2 association can persist outside the sparse low-9p21 region and therefore helps distinguish CDKN2A-specific signal from possible copy-number-region context; an attenuated result would not reject the core association but would weaken specificity. The combined adherent-culture plus high-ROC-screen robustness tests do not create new biology; they test whether the six core associations are merely driven by dominant culture or high-quality-screen subsets. These remain dataset-level associations in the supplied lung-focused resource, not causal, therapeutic, or externally generalizable claims.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
All newly delivered results are discovery Welch analyses in the supplied dataset; independent validation capacity is exhausted. Estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. I continue to treat roughly 0.10 absolute dependency-score units as a conservative practical benchmark, together with interval precision and consistency with the established core effects.

H317 and H322-H327 support the six core dataset-level associations under dominant adherent culture plus high screen-quality restriction. SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high WRN dependency, TP53-loss weaker USP7 dependency, KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency, CDKN2A-loss stronger MDM2 dependency, and PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 dependency all have large, precise signed effects in H322-H327. H317 additionally shows that the MSI-high WRN effect remains very strong in the SLFN11-high/high-ROC subset. These are not external replications, but they reduce concern that the core associations are driven by culture context or low-quality screen subsets.

The QC-refined interaction probes are less convincing. H316 remains a suggestive SLFN11-high enhancement of the MSI-high WRN association: signed interaction +0.078 with 95% CI +0.006 to +0.150. It excludes the null, but the point estimate is below the practical benchmark, the interval is wide, the lower bound is close to zero, and this is one of many exploratory interaction tests. I therefore leave it unresolved and closed rather than accepting a context-amplification claim.

H318-H320 are imprecise refinements of prior STAT3-PTEN context hypotheses. H318 high-ploidy signed interaction is +0.083 with CI including zero. H319 IFN-gamma-high signed interaction is +0.095, just below the practical benchmark, with CI including zero. H320 EMT-high signed interaction is +0.102, above the practical benchmark but with CI including zero and wide uncertainty. Given multiplicity, no validation, and loss of precision after restriction to high-quality screens, I leave these unresolved and closed; they do not justify upgrading context-modification claims beyond what is already cautiously supported by the earlier unstratified analyses.

H321 is not estimable because of insufficient cells after conditioning on copy_number_9p21 not below the median. This is an absence of evidence, not evidence of absence. The CDKN2A-loss MDM2 association remains accepted in the broader dataset and in other strata, but the requested copy-number specificity check remains unresolved and closed.

Overall, the new robustness tests reinforce the six core dataset-level associations and identify no reliable new context-specific enhancement that can be accepted without external replication.

Several accepted PTEN-STAT3 context effects remain imprecise, especially EMT H179, and AXL, stemness, TP53, and KEAP1 contexts remain unresolved or near-null. Third, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, signed +0.802 CI 0.782 to 0.822 and validated +0.800 CI 0.769 to 0.831, robust across strata. Fourth, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, signed +0.796 CI 0.776 to 0.816 and validated high-quality +0.799 CI 0.759 to 0.839, stable across contexts. Fifth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, signed +0.267 CI 0.215 to 0.319 and validated +0.283 CI 0.208 to 0.358; dataset-level enhancement is accepted for IFN-gamma-high lines, interaction +0.212 CI 0.094 to 0.331, and EMT-high lines, interaction +0.141 CI 0.011 to 0.271, although EMT and several context refinements are imprecise. Sixth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, signed +0.117 CI 0.082 to 0.152 and validated +0.116 CI 0.065 to 0.166, reproducible across libraries, QC subsets, lineage, ploidy, expression, co-alterations, and the MTAP-loss TP53-intact subset; this is the smallest core effect but crosses the practical benchmark. Negative findings are broad. Self-driver dependency hypotheses are unsupported: BRAF V600E does not strengthen BRAF dependency, KRAS mutation does not strengthen KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification does not strengthen EGFR dependency, and ERBB2 amplification does not strengthen ERBB2 dependency; EGFR amplification failed independent validation, ERBB2 amplification remained null, and the initial RB1-loss DHX9 signal did not replicate. Cross-receptor and co-alteration analyses were mostly null, including ERBB2 amplification with STAT3 or EGFR dependency, EGFR amplification with ERBB2 or TMED10 dependency, and most MYC amplification contrasts across USP7, POLR2A, DHX9, RPL11, STAT3, KIF18A, TMED10, and WRN within MSI-low lines. TP53 loss did not affect MDM2 or RPL11, MTAP loss did not provide a robust independent MDM2 effect, and constructed markers D, E, and F showed no consistent core associations. Robustness and context-modification screens generally did not yield additional reliable enhancements. Examples include failure of ERBB2 amplification to support STAT3 dependency, rejection of MYC interaction for STAT3 and MDM2, rejection of SLFN11 interaction for STAT3, and near-null or rejected context contrasts for USP7, NFE2L2, SMARCA2, WRN, and MDM2 in many tested media, lineage, co-alteration, expression, and screen-quality strata. The accepted context-enhancement claims are limited to PTEN-loss STAT3 in IFN-gamma-high and EMT-high lines, and the EMT claim is imprecise. Unresolved uncertainty remains in a small set of context probes. The SLFN11-high enhancement of MSI-high WRN dependency is suggestive but below the practical benchmark in both all-screen and high-quality screens, with signed interactions +0.061 CI 0.002 to 0.119 and +0.078 CI 0.006 to 0.150. The high-ploidy STAT3-PTEN interaction is positive but compatible with null, and high-quality STAT3-PTEN ploidy, IFN, and EMT refinements remain imprecise. CDKN2A-MDM2 cannot be cleanly separated from 9p21 copy-number biology because the requested low-9p21 exclusions were sparse and non-estimable. WRN in low mutation-burden subsets was also non-estimable rather than negative. Several pre-registered marker and STK11 main-effect comparisons, including POLR2A-STK11 and some research-marker tests, were never analyzed because capacity was exhausted. Overall, the evidence supports six dataset-level associations in this supplied lung-focused resource, with validated reproducibility for the core effects but no validated independent context interactions. These are associations only and do not establish causality, therapeutic relevance, or external generalizability. The most informative next analysis is external replication using larger independent cohorts that jointly model the six markers and contextual co-alterations; priority analyses should jointly model CDKN2A, MTAP, and 9p21 copy-number states for MDM2, jointly model MSI, SLFN11, mutation burden, and screen QC for WRN, and assess PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency with IFN-gamma, EMT, ploidy, and expression context using joint interaction or mixed subgroup models."}
